questions.prompt: Where does the middleware file live and how many are there per project?

options.text: A single middleware.ts at the project root (or src/)
One middleware.ts in every route folder

questions.explanation: There is one middleware.ts entry point at the project root (or inside src/).

questions.prompt: Which config key scopes middleware to specific paths? export const config = { ______: [...] }
questions.explanation: config.matcher limits which request paths the middleware runs on.

questions.prompt: Which are true about middleware? Select all that apply.

options.text: It runs before the request is completed (before rendering)
It runs on the Edge runtime by default
It should be fast and avoid heavy database work
It is a complete substitute for authorization at the data layer

questions.explanation: Middleware runs early on the Edge runtime and must be fast. It's a coarse gate, not a replacement for real authorization near your data.

questions.prompt: Match each NextResponse call to its effect.

pairs.right: Send the browser to a new URL
Serve a different path, URL unchanged

questions.explanation: next() proceeds, redirect() navigates, rewrite() serves another path silently, and setting headers modifies the response.

questions.prompt: Order how a request to /dashboard flows through an auth middleware.

items.text: A request to /dashboard matches the middleware matcher
Middleware checks for a session cookie
If present, NextResponse.next() lets the page render

questions.explanation: The matcher triggers the middleware, which checks the cookie and either redirects or lets the request continue.
